Evans-Jensen lecture classification: 4

A patient has a three-part intertrochanteric fracture with a separate lesser trochanter fragment and loss of medial support. Under the supplied lecture’s Evans-Jensen notation, which category best describes the separated lesser-trochanter pattern?

  1. Grade 1B in the supplied lecture scheme
  2. Grade 2A in the supplied lecture scheme
  3. Grade 3 in the supplied lecture scheme
  4. Grade 2B in the supplied lecture scheme
  5. Grade 1A in the supplied lecture scheme
Answer and explanation

Grade 2B in the supplied lecture scheme

A three-part fracture with a separate lesser trochanter is grade 2B in this notation.

Option explanations

Grade 2B in the supplied lecture scheme: A three-part fracture with a separate lesser trochanter is grade 2B in this notation.

Grade 1A in the supplied lecture scheme: A two-part nondisplaced intertrochanteric fracture is grade 1A in this lecture’s Evans-Jensen notation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Grade 1B in the supplied lecture scheme: A displaced two-part intertrochanteric fracture is grade 1B; it can be stable after adequate reduction. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Grade 2A in the supplied lecture scheme: A three-part fracture with a separate greater trochanter is grade 2A in this notation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Grade 3 in the supplied lecture scheme: A four-part intertrochanteric pattern is grade 3 in the supplied lecture scheme. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
